newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says no U.S. request for base against Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says no U.S. request for base against Iraq.

text.p: Turkey said on Thursday it had not received any request from NATO ally the United States for the use of an air base on Turkish soil to strike Iraq.
"There has been no request," a foreign ministry official said. "They obviously don't need it at the present," he told Reuters.
U.S. planes have moved into position for possible bombing raids against Iraq after Baghdad forces fired a surface-to-air missile at U.S. fighters over northern Iraq on Wednesday.

Eight U.S. F-117A jets have flown to Kuwait and four B-52s moved from Guam in the Pacific Ocean to a British air base on the Indian Ocean island of Diego Garcia to be in closer striking range to Iraq, U.S. officials said.
The Iraqi SAM-6 missile fired on Wednesday missed the U.S. planes which were from a Western allied air force that flies out of Incirlik air base near the southern Turkish city of Adana.
